Origin: reflect full from #4596

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md` (the tombstone-PR path, lines ~263-294) still carries a prose copy of the PR body's `### Resume` line grammar: it tells the agent to read the `### Resume` section, find the exact command line `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR="{run-dir}" /claude-tweaks:flow ...`, and validate the marker by eye.

Record #4596 moved the same grammar into code: `plugin/bin/lib/flow/pr-body.js` exports `resumeLineUnder(body)` (last `### Resume` heading) and `parseResumeLine(line, runId)` (allowlisted dir and target classes, a string `runId` guard, no `..` dir segment), and `plugin/bin/stale-claim-pr.js` prints `resume` only for a line `parseResumeLine` accepts. The tombstone path in `claim-targets.md` is the last prose restatement, so the two can drift (the #4596 review found `RESUME_LINE_RE`'s original denylist passing `!` and C0 control characters, which the prose copy would also accept).

Found by the #4596 whole-branch review; out of that record's two named prose files.

## Deliverables

Route the tombstone-PR `### Resume` read in `plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md` through `pr-body.js`'s `resumeLineUnder`/`parseResumeLine` (a small CLI or an existing one such as `stale-claim-pr.js --resume`), so the prose no longer restates the grammar.

Extend the existing conformance test that pins `claim-targets.md` as the only prose copy (`tests/issue-claims-stale-open-pr-conformance.test.js`) so it pins the removal.

## Acceptance Criteria

`grep -F "### Resume" plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md` no longer shows prose that spells out the Resume line's shape; it names the CLI/function instead (run first against the current tree and seen to match).

A tombstone PR whose `### Resume` line fails `parseResumeLine` (for example one containing `!`) routes to the resolve path, with a test that is red on the old prose.

`npm test` passes.

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md` — replace the prose Resume-line grammar with a call to the shared parser
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/pr-body.js` — parser the prose should route through
- `tests/issue-claims-stale-open-pr-conformance.test.js` — pin the removal

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/plan-audit.js --task-markers {plan}` reads each task's optional `**Role:**` / `**Review risk:**` markers (#3378) and prints `{"markers", "tasks": [{index, title, role, risk}], "findings"?}`. `/build`'s per-task tier forwarding (`plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md`, the "Per-task role/review-risk tier forwarding (#3378)" paragraph) is its one consumer: a task reported `risk: "high"` gets a Capable task review; `risk: null` falls back to the run's `size:`-derived tier.

The parser (`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/parser.js`, `extractTaskMarkers`) captures everything after the key to end of line (`RISK_MARKER_RE = /^\*\*Review risk:\*\*[ \t]*(.*)$/m`, same shape for `ROLE_MARKER_RE`), trims it, and recognizes it only on an exact whole-value match against the closed sets `TASK_MARKER_RISKS = ['high']` / `TASK_MARKER_ROLES = ['transcription', 'integration', 'judgment']`. So `**Review risk:** high (a read-once/write-last ordering, and branching on computed state)` yields `riskRaw = "high (a read-once/…)"`, `risk: null`. The same holds for a `**Role:** judgment (needs design judgment)` line.

The mis-parse is then invisible end to end:

- `checkTaskMarkers` (`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`) records a `findings` entry, but `--task-markers` (`plugin/bin/plan-audit.js`) only embeds it in the stdout JSON — exit 0, nothing on stderr. `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` documents findings as warn-only, never exit-changing.
- `dispatch.md`'s tier-forwarding paragraph never reads `findings` at all — it keys only on `markers` and each task's `role`/`risk`.
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` documents the syntax as `**Review risk:** high` but never says the value must stand alone on the line, and a trailing reason reads as valid to a human author.

Net effect: a task its author explicitly marked high-risk silently drops from a Capable review to the unpinned tier. Putting the reason on its own line (`**Review risk:** high`, then `Why: …`) parses correctly — confirmed by the reporter on plugin 6.156.1.

**Related:** #3986, #4618, #4549, #4559 (near-duplicate screen: shared Key Files / body anchors only — no title similarity; #4618 adds a different risk axis to plan-audit and shares `plan-audit.js`/`checks.js`)

## Deliverables

1. **Accept a trailing annotation after a recognized marker value.** In `extractTaskMarkers`, a `**Role:**` / `**Review risk:**` value is recognized when its leading token is in the closed set and is either the whole value or is followed by whitespace (the annotation after it is ignored). `**Review risk:** high (reason)` → `risk: "high"`; `**Role:** judgment — needs design judgment` → `role: "judgment"`. A leading token not in the closed set (`medium`, `hgih`, `high-ish`) stays unrecognized (`null`) exactly as today. `roleRaw`/`riskRaw` keep carrying the full raw trimmed line value.
2. **Make an unrecognized marker value visible on stderr.** When `--task-markers` produces any `findings` entry, print one warning line per finding to stderr naming the task index, title, field, and raw value (e.g. `plan-audit.js: warning: task 3 "X" — unrecognized Review risk value "medium"; the task reads as unmarked`). Stdout JSON and the exit code (0) are unchanged — findings stay warn-only per `plan-audit.md`.
3. **Surface findings in `/build`'s tier forwarding.** `dispatch.md`'s Per-task role/review-risk tier forwarding paragraph: when the `--task-markers` output carries `findings`, log one decision-log line naming each offending task/field/value (via `log-decision.js`, status per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s Status semantics — not `STAGED`, since nothing is staged) and continue dispatch with those tasks treated as unmarked — never a stop.
4. **Document the accepted shape.** `plan-authoring-checks.md`'s marker paragraph and `plan-audit.md`'s `--task-markers` paragraph state that a trailing annotation after the value is allowed and ignored, and that an unrecognized value is now warned on stderr as well as listed in `findings`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node plugin/bin/plan-audit.js --task-markers plan.md` on a plan with `### Task 1: X` followed by `**Review risk:** high (a read-once/write-last ordering, and branching on computed state)` prints task 1 with `"risk": "high"`, no `findings` key, exit 0.
- The same for `**Role:** judgment (needs design judgment)` → `"role": "judgment"`, and for a value followed by an em-dash annotation (`**Review risk:** high — reason`).
- `**Review risk:** high` and `**Role:** transcription` with no annotation still parse exactly as today (existing `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/parser.test.js` / `cli.test.js` #3378 cases stay green unmodified).
- `**Review risk:** medium`, `**Review risk:** high-ish`, and `**Role:** trivial` still yield `null` plus a `findings` entry carrying the full raw value; `--task-markers` exits 0 and writes one stderr warning line per finding naming the task index, field, and raw value.
- A plan with no findings writes nothing to stderr under `--task-markers`.
- `dispatch.md`'s tier-forwarding paragraph names the `findings` field and the decision-log line it writes; `tests/plan-task-markers-conformance.test.js` (or a sibling conformance test) pins that the paragraph references `findings`.
- `plan-authoring-checks.md` and `plan-audit.md` each state that a trailing annotation after the marker value is ignored.
- New unit tests in `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/parser.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/cli.test.js` cover the annotated forms and the stderr warning, and each goes red when the parser change (respectively the stderr write) is reverted.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fix plan-audit's task markers silently ignoring `**Review risk:** high` when a reason follows the value on the same line, and warn about unrecognized marker values instead of dropping them quietly.

## Technical Approach

Parser: keep `ROLE_MARKER_RE` / `RISK_MARKER_RE` capturing the full line (so `roleRaw`/`riskRaw` and the findings' `value` stay the raw text), then derive the recognized value from the leading token — e.g. `const lead = raw.split(/\s/, 1)[0]` and recognize `lead` when it is in the closed set. Splitting on whitespace (not on any non-word character) is what keeps `high-ish` / `high,` unrecognized rather than read as `high`; decide in the build whether a directly-attached separator like `high,` should also be accepted, and test whichever way it lands. `checkTaskMarkers` must use the same recognition rule as `extractTaskMarkers` (today it re-tests `TASK_MARKER_RISKS.includes(t.riskRaw)` against the raw value — switch it to test the recognized `t.risk`/`t.role` being null while the raw is non-null, so an annotated valid value is not reported as a finding).

CLI: in the `parsed.taskMarkers` branch of `plan-audit.js`, after computing `findings`, write each to `process.stderr` before the stdout JSON line; leave `process.exitCode` untouched.

Skill prose: the `dispatch.md` change is one sentence inside the existing tier-forwarding paragraph; keep the `markers: false` branch byte-for-byte as the paragraph promises.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/parser.js` — `extractTaskMarkers`: leading-token recognition for Role / Review risk
- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js` — `checkTaskMarkers`: finding iff raw present and recognized value null
- `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js` — `--task-markers` branch: one stderr warning line per finding
- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` — tier-forwarding paragraph: log `findings` to the decision log, continue with the task unmarked
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — marker paragraph: trailing annotation allowed and ignored
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` — `--task-markers` paragraph: annotation rule + stderr warning
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/parser.test.js` — annotated-value cases
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/checks.test.js` — annotated valid value yields no finding
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/cli.test.js` — stdout risk/role + stderr warning cases
- `tests/plan-task-markers-conformance.test.js` — pin `dispatch.md`'s `findings` handling

## Gotchas

- `tests/plan-task-markers-conformance.test.js` pins the marker syntax in `plan-authoring-checks.md` with `/\*\*Review risk:\*\* (\S+)`/` and the dispatch tier wording — edit the prose so those pins still match, or update the pins in the same change.
- The `markers` flag semantics are unchanged: a recognized key with an unrecognized value still sets `markers: true`.
- Keep the matcher same-line-only (`[ \t]*`, never `\s*`) — `parser.js`'s own comment explains why `\s` would read into the next line.
- Exit code for findings must stay 0 — `plan-audit.md` documents findings as warn-only and `dispatch.md` runs this call unconditionally before SDD dispatch.

## Original request

plan-audit: --task-markers reads '**Review risk:** high (reason)' as no risk, silently

**Summary:** `plan-audit.js --task-markers` reads a `**Review risk:** high` line that has a trailing reason as no risk, with no warning.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/plan-audit.js --task-markers` (with `skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`'s marker paragraph and `skills/build/dispatch.md`'s per-task tier forwarding)

**Repro steps:**
1. Write a plan with `### Task 1: X`, followed by the line `**Review risk:** high (a read-once/write-last ordering, and branching on computed state)`.
2. Run `node bin/plan-audit.js --task-markers plan.md`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: task 1 reports `"risk": "high"`, or the CLI exits non-zero or warns, naming the task and the unparsed value.
Actual: task 1 reports `"risk": null`. A `findings` entry quotes the raw value, but the exit code is 0 and nothing is printed to stderr. `/build`'s per-task tier forwarding keys on `risk: "high"`, so the task's review would silently drop from Capable to the unpinned tier. The marker reads as valid to a human, so the degradation is invisible. Putting the reason on its own line (`**Review risk:** high`, then `Why: …`) gives `"risk": "high"`.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1

## Current State

On a base:{ref} whole-branch scope the own-work filter drops shipping work: it treats any file absent from the first-parent walk as arriving from {base}, but the base is a tag. In this range #4587, #4423 and #4466 sit on the second parent of first-parent merges, so following the rule would have excluded 32 non-run-dir paths from the release gate.

Found at `plugin/skills/review/merge-provenance-check.md:15` by the release-gate review of v6.157.0 (range v6.156.3...3470ac15c).

## Deliverables

Fix the defect at `plugin/skills/review/merge-provenance-check.md:15`, with a regression test.

## Acceptance Criteria

Origin: /claude-tweaks:specify #4552 brainstorm

Defer-reason: tangential

Surface: backend

**Related:** #4552, #4108, #2251, #2580, #2581, #2582, #4199

## Current State

A bundled merge lists every record in its `Fixes` footer, but its subject carries one `(#N)` suffix: the lowest record's (`plugin/bin/lib/release/subject.js`). Three release surfaces read only that one record.

- **Records shipped:** `plugin/skills/release/console.md:20` builds the row from "One line per `(#N)` suffix", and `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js:323` passes each commit's `subject` with no body. That row says a record silently absent "would under-report what the release contains".
- **Bookkeeping:** `plugin/skills/release/bookkeeping.md:19` builds the shipped set from the same suffix, so Step 7's `Shipped in v{version}` comment skips the other bundled records. They still close through their `Fixes` lines at merge.
- **Release notes:** `plugin/bin/lib/compose-subject.js:336` renders only the lowest record's Release Note, and `RELEASE_NOTE_FOOTER_RE` in `plugin/bin/lib/release-notes.js:16` reads one `Release-Note:` line per commit. The composer still requires a note from every bundled record.

**Measured on `main` (2026-10-30):**

- 72 of the 620 composed merges in the last 1,500 commits were bundles.
- Across eight released bundles, seven suffix records got a `Shipped in v` comment (7 of 7) and the other bundled records got none (0 of 18). The eighth bundle had no suffix match.
- 13 non-suffix records sampled from v6.156.2, v6.153.0 and v6.152.0: all 10 with a real note were missing from the Release, for example #4421 and #4041. The other 3 say "No user-visible change". Their numbers do appear, on the suffix commit's `closes` line, with no note text.
- In v6.156.2, 4 of the 6 Highlights bullets say "No user-visible change".

**Why the rule exists:** "never aggregated" is not a design principle. #2580 lists rendering every bundled note as a non-goal, calls it "an accepted scope limitation", and names multiple `Release-Note:` lines per commit as the way to solve it. #2581 repeats it as a known limitation.

**A related defect, from reading the code:** a merge composed with `--keep-open` on its lowest record has a `Refs` line but its suffix still names that record, so Step 7 books it and closes it, against #4199's intent. No release has been checked for a live case. This record's shipped-set rule fixes it.

**Decisions (human-approved 2026-10-30):**

- **Shipped set:** a commit with any `Fixes` or `Refs` line ships its `Fixes` numbers. A commit with neither keeps the `(#N)` suffix rule. A `Refs` record is not booked, because Step 7 closes what it books.
- **Notes:** one `Release-Note:` line per record, including a kept-open record, whose code did ship. Not an agent-written bundle note: #2580 says a note is written once, at spec time, by whoever holds the record's context, and makes release-time rewording a non-goal.
- **Filtering belongs in the renderer**, not the composer, so it also clears the noise from single-record merges and the commit keeps every note.
- **No backfill.** Old records would get comments long after the fact, and old Releases would change without anyone expecting it.

## Deliverables

1. `plugin/bin/lib/compose-subject.js` passes every record's Release Note to `composeSubject`, lowest number first, and `plugin/bin/lib/release/subject.js` writes one `Release-Note:` line per note. A single-record merge composes a byte-identical title and body to today. Update both header comments, which state the old rule.
2. `plugin/bin/lib/release-notes.js` gains one shared extractor that returns every `Release-Note:` line in a commit body, trimmed and in order. `plugin/bin/lib/release-local/commits.js` and `plugin/bin/lib/release-notes-publish.js` both use it, so neither restates the pattern. Parsed commits carry all the notes.
3. `renderReleaseNotes` renders every note and drops, case-insensitively, any note starting with `No user-visible change`. It also removes exact duplicates within the release, and still returns `null` when nothing is left.
4. `plugin/bin/lib/release-local/commits.js`'s `parseCommit` reads the `Fixes #N` and `Refs #N` lines (whole-line matches) into two number lists, and `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js`'s `unreleased` probe passes both through on each commit.
5. `plugin/skills/release/console.md`'s Records shipped row and `plugin/skills/release/bookkeeping.md`'s shipped set use the Decisions' shipped-set rule. Numbers are still deduplicated across commits, and a number whose payload is a pull request is still dropped. `Refs` numbers that nothing else ships render on one nested `Kept open (not booked)` console line.
6. Update `docs/releasing.md` and `docs/journeys/merge-a-record-with-a-conventional-subject-2251.md` wherever they state one note per merge.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `compose-subject.js 10,11,12` on a fixture bundle produces a body with three `Release-Note:` lines in number order, then the `Fixes` lines. With `--keep-open 11`, it still has three notes, and #11's footer line is `Refs #11`.
2. `compose-subject.js 10` output equals today's for the same fixture, compared byte for byte in a test.
3. A bundle where any record has an empty `## Release Note` section still fails with the existing message.
4. The shared extractor returns every note from a three-note body and `[]` from a body with none. `parseCommit` and `parseReleaseNotesFromLog` both return all three for the same body.
5. `renderReleaseNotes` drops `No user-visible change.` and `No user-visible change: fixes Windows-only test failures.`, keeps a note that only mentions that phrase later in its text, collapses an exact duplicate to one bullet, and returns `null` when every note was dropped.
6. Given a fixture range with a three-record bundle, `release-notes-publish.js`'s run applies a Highlights block holding all three notes to both the Release body and the CHANGELOG entry. With only `No user-visible change` notes in range, it is a no-op on both targets.
7. The `unreleased` probe returns `fixes` and `refs` for each commit: `[10, 12]` and `[11]` for a bundle with #11 kept open, and two empty lists for a commit with neither line.
8. Prose tests pin the shipped-set rule in `console.md` and `bookkeeping.md`, including the three cases: a bundle books every `Fixes` number, a `Refs`-only commit books nothing even when its suffix names that record, and a commit with neither line books its suffix.
9. Revert the composer change, the extractor change, the renderer filter and the `fixes`/`refs` read in turn, and show which new test fails for each.
10. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

A release now lists every record in a bundled merge, carries each one's own release note, and leaves out notes that say there is no user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

The composer change is small because every note is already validated at `compose-subject.js:330`: replace the one-note read with a per-record read. Have the new lines replace the single push at `subject.js:108`, keeping the existing paragraph order so `Release-Note:` still comes before the footers. Look at `parseFixesSpan` in `plugin/bin/lib/flow/closing-links.js` before writing the `Fixes`/`Refs` read; reuse it if it fits a commit body.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/compose-subject.js` — one note per record
- `plugin/bin/lib/release/subject.js` — one line per note
- `plugin/bin/lib/release-notes.js` — shared extractor and renderer filter
- `plugin/bin/lib/release-notes-publish.js` — reads through the extractor
- `plugin/bin/lib/release-local/commits.js` — all notes, plus `Fixes`/`Refs`
- `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js` — `fixes` and `refs` on each commit
- `plugin/skills/release/console.md` — Records shipped row
- `plugin/skills/release/bookkeeping.md` — shipped set
- `docs/releasing.md` — release note wording
- `docs/journeys/merge-a-record-with-a-conventional-subject-2251.md` — bundle wording
- `tests/bin-lib/compose-subject.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/release/subject.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/release-notes.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/release-notes-publish.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/release-local/commits.test.js` — the cases above
- `tests/merge-subject-composer-conformance.test.js` — existing pins

## Gotchas

- `tests/bin-lib/compose-subject.test.js` pins a non-subject note as validated but not rendered (#2580's AC 3). That pin flips here on purpose.
- An older installed build reads only the first `Release-Note:` line and the suffix, so a new-format commit reads as it does today. Nothing breaks during rollout.
- #4552 edits the same composer and `subject.js` title logic. The two touch different paragraphs, but whichever merges second must re-run the composer tests against the other.
- release-please lists the `closes` numbers by parsing the commit body. Never test this with a live release (#2582). Keep the `Fixes` lines in their own paragraph, then confirm on the first real release that a bundle's `closes` numbers still appear.
- A `release: published` re-fire for a release published before this ships renders a different block, so the idempotency check would not match and a second Highlights block could be added. Only the newest release is ever walked, so this window closes with the next release.
- The filter depends on how authors phrase a note, so a differently worded "internal only" note still shows. That is no worse than today.
- A `Refs` record shipping in two merges would otherwise show its note twice, which is why the renderer removes duplicates.

## Original request

> Origin: /claude-tweaks:specify #4552 brainstorm
>
> Defer-reason: tangential
>
> **Related:** #4552, #2251, #2581
>
> ## Current State
>
> A bundled merge lists every record in its `Fixes` footer, but its subject carries one `(#N)` suffix: the lowest record's (`plugin/bin/lib/release/subject.js`). Three release surfaces read only that one record. This comes from reading the prose and code; no release has been checked for it.
>
> - **Records shipped:** `plugin/skills/release/console.md:20` builds the row from "One line per `(#N)` suffix", and `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js:323` passes each commit's `subject` with no body. That row says a record silently absent "would under-report what the release contains".
> - **Bookkeeping:** `plugin/skills/release/bookkeeping.md:19` builds the shipped set from the same suffix, so Step 7's `Shipped in v{version}` comment skips the other bundled records. They still close through their `Fixes` lines at merge.
> - **Release notes:** `plugin/bin/lib/compose-subject.js` renders only the lowest record's Release Note, deliberately ("never aggregated across a bundle"), and `plugin/bin/lib/release-notes.js` reads one `Release-Note:` line per commit. So the other records' notes do not reach the changelog, although the composer requires each to have one.
>
> ## Deliverables
>
> - [ ] Decide how the release reads a bundle's records, and how a bundle's release notes reach the changelog.
> - [ ] Implement that in the release pack, `console.md`, `bookkeeping.md`, and the composer or notes renderer, with a test per surface.

> ## Open Question

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Overview

Replace wrap-up's Verification Brief with an **acceptance packet** for every project — universal, not gated on control mode. The packet is what the human finds at the acceptance control point: it makes validating a finished feature cheap, and it is the only artifact `/accept` and Dispatch both read. Control mode (separate units) later adds the stop-removing behaviors; the packet itself is a plain improvement that ships for everyone, migrated expand-contract.

Sections, in order (design section 6):

1. **What changed** — user-facing summary, not a diff tour.
2. **Recording** — the walkthrough of the feature in use (filled by the recording record; a placeholder section here).
3. **Test guide** — numbered manual steps, each with a direct link that lands in the right state (role, test data). Credentials are referenced by vault entry name, never embedded as session tokens or passwords.
4. **Couldn't test** — what the agent could not verify and why (no backend, no dev server, needs a real device, needs real credentials). **A check that skipped itself is listed here, never shown as silence.**
5. **Tried to break** — the negative stories and edge cases run, with results.
6. **Least confident** — where the agent's judgment is weakest ("if I were you I'd poke here"); sourced from review's low-confidence findings.
7. **Risk proofs** — present only when risk flags were kept (the specific evidence per flag; filled by the risk-flag record).
8. **Decisions left for you** — carried-forward items (filled by the control-mode records); omitted when empty.
9. **Deploy status** — target and, for `dev`, whether the feature is confirmed live (filled by the dev-target record; for `local` it states the target).

**Canonical copy:** a marker-block comment on the work record (a GitHub comment; the PR links to it). The run-dir copy is a working copy and is never read after the run. **One packet per work item; re-posting updates the same comment in place** (find by marker, edit by comment id), never a second comment. **Fact-validated narration:** every claim in sections 3-7 cites a gathered fact (story report, screenshot, test output, review finding) and the citations are validated against the gathered fact set, following the repo's gather / narrate / render pattern as `/activity` implements it (`plugin/bin/lib/activity/gather.js` and `render.js`; the `fact-validated-narration` skill is the checklist).

Anti-goals this record carries: a "tested X" claim with no run behind it; a skipped check that shows as nothing; packet links that point at a build lacking the feature (deploy status owns that); secrets reaching a public surface (the recording record owns redaction, but this record must never embed credential-shaped values in the Test guide).

**Contract decisions this record pins (the packet contract file states them; later records cite it):**

- **Marker and lookup.** The canonical comment carries `<!-- acceptance-packet: v1 -->` on its first line (registered in `_shared/pr-run-comments.md`'s marker registry). A writer lists the work record's comments, keeps those that carry the marker and pass `comment-trust.js`, and edits the earliest by comment id; extra marker comments are reported, never edited or deleted. If the matched comment cannot be edited by the current identity, the run reports that visibly and posts nothing (never a second packet). The PR gets one idempotently appended body line `Acceptance packet: {comment url}`; with no PR (the `local-merge` model) there is no link and none is needed. Under `local-files` the packet lives in the record body between `<!-- acceptance-packet:start -->` and `<!-- acceptance-packet:end -->` and is replaced in place between the delimiters.
- **Facts and claims.** A fact is `{ id, kind, status, reason?, source }` with `kind` one of `change`, `check`, `story`, `finding`, `link`, `recording`, `flag`, `decision`, `deploy`; `status` one of `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `not-run`; ids are stable strings such as `check:unit-tests` or `story:login#negative-2`. A claim is `{ section, text, refs[] }` with `section` one of `what-changed`, `test-guide`, `tried-to-break`, `least-confident`, `risk-proofs`. Section-to-kind table (in the contract): what-changed cites `change`; test-guide cites `story` and `link`; tried-to-break cites `story` and `check`; least-confident cites `finding`; risk-proofs cites `flag` plus the proof fact. Sections 2 (Recording), 8 (Decisions) and 9 (Deploy status) render facts of kind `recording`, `decision` and `deploy` directly and are not narrated claims. `schemaVersion: 1` is one constant used by the facts file and the marker alike; later records add fact kinds only by extending the contract's table.
- **Validation policy: visible drop.** `validatePacket` drops any claim whose `refs` is empty, names an absent fact, or names a fact incompatible with the claim, and the packet always states `N claims were dropped for missing evidence` (and lists them in the run-dir working copy). It never posts silently thinner. Compatibility: a claim asserting verification (tested, verified, works) may cite only `passed` facts; a claim citing a `failed` fact renders under Tried to break with the failure; one citing `skipped` or `not-run` moves to Couldn't test.
- **The expected check set comes from outside the facts.** Gather derives the checks and stories expected for the work (the spec's Acceptance Criteria and verify expectations, the planned stories) independently of what ran; an expected check with no result fact renders under Couldn't test as `not run`, so a self-skipped check cannot be silent. Gather is `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/packet-gather.js` (deterministic; a partial gather renders a stated `partial` note); narration is an LLM step in the wrap-up prose; wrap-up runs gather, narrate, validate, render, post in that order.
- **Failure contract.** If the post or edit fails, the pending acceptance label is not applied and the failure is reported. The reader function `readPacket(comments)` in the same module applies the reader rules: an unknown `schemaVersion` reads as unreadable (stated, no second packet), duplicates resolve to the earliest trusted comment, an untrusted-author marker is ignored, and the run-dir copy is never consulted (a test proves a stale local copy is ignored).
- **Links.** Test-guide links must be http(s) on the local base URL host or the `dev-base-url` host only; any other host is refused. A shared constant defines the credential-shaped key set, matched case-insensitively after normalization in query, fragment and userinfo: `token`, `access_token`, `password`, `passwd`, `secret`, `session`, `sessionid`, `jwt`, `auth`, `key`, `api_key`, `sig`, `signature`, `x-amz-signature`. The Recording record reuses this one constant for its redactor. When the deploy section is not confirmed live, each Test-guide link carries `(link unverified: deploy not confirmed live)`.
- **Facts-poor and infra items.** A section with nothing to say renders one line stating why (`not applicable: no UI surface`), never an empty heading. For `Surface: infra`/`backend` work the Test guide lists commands to run instead of links. For decomposed work the packet lives on the parent (the feature-acceptance record owns the gate); a sub-issue's wrap-up posts nothing and the existing parent-gate routing stands.
- **Size.** The renderer caps the comment at 60,000 characters (GitHub's limit is 65,536) and truncates by omitting whole items with a stated `truncated: N items omitted` line.
- **Section 1 is cited too.** `what-changed` claims cite `change` facts (changed files, commits), so every narrated section is validated.
- **Old brief.** All five Routing call sites land in `verification-brief.md`, so replacing its template migrates them at once; the old section map (The ask to What changed; What shipped to What changed; Confirmed to Test guide and Tried to break; Observation plan to Test guide) is a table in the contract. Briefs already posted stay readable through `plugin/skills/demo/legacy-brief-compatibility.md` (kept until the final cleanup record). A work item with only a legacy brief comment gets a new packet comment; the legacy comment is left untouched, and "exactly one" applies to packet comments.

## Non-Goals

- Not posting the recording or redaction (separate record), not deploy-status refresh (dev-target record), not the control-mode "Decisions left for you" population (control-mode records) — this record defines the sections and renders them when data exists.
- Not the `/accept` skill or the verdict handler.
- Not Dispatch's display of the packet.
- Not removing the legacy-brief reader (`demo/legacy-brief-compatibility.md`); the five call sites in `verification-brief.md`'s Routing table keep working and now land on the packet.

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| — | none intra-batch | — |

## Current State

- The Verification Brief: `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief.md` (about 31 KB). Its `## Routing` section lists five call sites (wrap-up Phase 4 acceptance-labeling, wrap-up's auto-merge short-circuit, dispatch's group auto-merge gate, dispatch close-out step 3, tidy's Open-parent-gate action). Its `## Verification Brief` template has sections The ask / What shipped / Confirmed / Observation plan. It already composes a **Try it block** for every record (`## Try it block`, backed by `plugin/skills/_shared/try-it.md`).
- Parent-gate: `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` (a decomposed sub-issue never carries its own pending label; its parent carries one gate). Feature-level acceptance for decomposed work is a separate record; here, keep the existing routing intact.
- Engine: `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-render.js` renders wrap-up output; `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` verifies it.
- Pattern to follow: `/activity` splits gather (`gh` to `facts.json`) / narrate / render, and `render.js` drops every `refs[]` citation not present in the facts (warning forms: `dropped citation`, `ambiguous citation`, `unparseable citation`), refuses a schemaVersion mismatch, and neutralizes newlines and link brackets in free text so a citation-shaped string in prose cannot forge a heading or link.
- Raw material: `/stories` negative stories, qa-agent step screenshots, review's low-confidence findings, `/walkthrough`'s GIF encoder.
- A shared contract file for the packet does not exist yet: `plugin/skills/_shared/acceptance-packet.md` is new.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `plugin/skills/_shared/acceptance-packet.md` (new): the packet contract — section list and order, the marker-block comment format and its find-by-marker/edit-in-place rule, the fact schema (what each of sections 3-7 may cite), the untrusted-content rules for free text, and which other units fill which sections.
- [ ] A packet builder module (pure, under `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/`) with `validatePacket(facts, narrative)` and `renderPacket(facts, narrative)`: drops or fails any claim in sections 3-7 whose citation is absent from the gathered facts; renders a skipped check under **Couldn't test**; neutralizes newlines and link brackets in narrative text per `/activity`'s `inline()` approach.
- [ ] Wrap-up posts exactly one packet comment per work item through the existing github write transport (`_shared/github-write-transport.md`), edits it in place on re-run, and links it from the PR; under `work-backend: local-files` it writes the packet into the record body section instead.
- [ ] `verification-brief.md` and `_shared/try-it.md` reworked so the Try it block and observation plan feed the packet's Test guide and Tried-to-break sections; the old brief sections are mapped, not silently dropped (a mapping table in the packet contract).
- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/packet-gather.js` (deterministic gather, partial-gather note) and `readPacket` (reader rules above) with the wrap-up prose that runs gather, narrate, validate, render, post in order; the PR-link line and the `local-files` delimiters from the contract decisions.
- [ ] Tests: validation rejects an uncited claim; a skipped check lands in Couldn't test; re-render with an existing marker comment edits rather than posts; schema mismatch is refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given facts containing a story report with one failed and one skipped check, `renderPacket` outputs the skipped check under `Couldn't test` (with its reason) and the failure under `Tried to break`; nothing is omitted silently (a test counts input checks against rendered rows).
2. A claim in the Test guide whose `refs` cites a fact id absent from the gathered facts is dropped by `validatePacket`, and the rendered packet states `1 claim was dropped for missing evidence`; a claim with no `refs` is dropped the same way; a "verified" claim citing a `failed` fact renders under Tried to break with the failure; one citing a `skipped` fact moves to Couldn't test. Each is pinned by a test.
2a. An expected check (derived from the spec's Acceptance Criteria or planned stories) with no result fact at all renders under Couldn't test as `not run`.
2b. `readPacket` returns the earliest trusted marker comment among duplicates, ignores an untrusted-author marker, reports `schemaVersion: 2` as unreadable, and never reads the run-dir copy.
2c. When the post or edit fails (fake runner returns an error) the pending acceptance label is not applied and the failure is reported.
2d. A packet that would exceed 60,000 characters is truncated by whole items with a `truncated: N items omitted` line.
3. Wrap-up's second run on a work item that already has a packet comment edits that comment (same comment id) and the work item ends with exactly one comment carrying the marker (test against the fake runner).
4. A narrative string containing `[x](https://evil.example)` or a forged `## Couldn't test` heading is rendered as inert prose (brackets escaped, newlines collapsed).
5. The packet contract states, and a conformance test pins, that credentials appear only as vault entry names and that the link rules above hold: a link to a host other than the local base URL host or `dev-base-url` is refused; a link carrying any key from the shared credential-key constant in its query, fragment or userinfo is refused after case and percent-encoding normalization (tests for `TOKEN=`, `tok%65n=`, `#sig=`, `user:pass@`, `sessionid=`); a benign `/docs/token-guide` path is accepted. For a `Surface: infra` record the Test guide lists commands and renders no links; sections with nothing to say render a one-line reason.
6. The five call sites in `verification-brief.md`'s Routing table still resolve and still apply the pending acceptance label; existing wrap-up tests pass unchanged apart from intended renames.
7. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Replaced the verification brief with an acceptance packet that lists what changed, how to test it, what could not be tested and where confidence is lowest, with every claim tied to evidence.

## Technical Approach

Three-stage gather / narrate / render. Gather is deterministic and writes a facts file in the run directory (working copy). The narration step is judgment and writes a narrative with `refs[]` per claim. The renderer is deterministic and trusts only the facts. The canonical copy is the posted comment, found by its marker and edited in place; the run-dir copy is never read afterward. The packet is the same artifact for control mode on or off — only which sections are populated differs.

### Data / API Surface

- Marker: a fenced marker block comment, versioned (`schemaVersion: 1`), following the repo's other marker-comment convention (`_shared/pr-run-comments.md`); author-trust-gated on read (`plugin/bin/lib/issues/comment-trust.js`).
- Facts: `{ checks[], stories[], findings[], links[], decisions[], deploy }` with stable ids that `refs[]` cite.
- Sections 2, 7, 8, 9 render a stated placeholder (`not recorded`, `no kept risk flags`, none, `target: local`) until their owning records populate them.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/acceptance-packet.md` — new packet contract
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief.md` — migrate to the packet; keep Routing
- `plugin/skills/_shared/try-it.md` — Try it block feeds the Test guide
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-render.js` — render integration
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/packet-gather.js` — new gather, `readPacket`, `validatePacket`, `renderPacket` (builder's split into sibling modules)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-run-comments.md` — register the `acceptance-packet` marker
- `plugin/bin/lib/activity/render.js` — reference pattern for citation validation (read, do not edit)
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/comment-trust.js` — trust gate for reading the marker comment
- `tests/try-it-contract-conformance.test.js` — pins the Try it contract; update with the move
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` — keep green

## Gotchas

- Replacing, not adding: two packets on one item is the failure mode; the old template is replaced in place in `verification-brief.md`, not kept beside the new one.
- Do not read the run-dir copy after the run; `/accept` and Dispatch read GitHub (AC 2b proves the reader ignores a stale local copy).
- The authenticated identity that posted the packet may differ on a re-run (cloud, Routine); AC 2c's failure path covers "cannot edit". Concurrent wrap-up runs on one record are prevented by the record claim; if one slips through, last write wins and the loser reports.
- The gather step must never silently pass a failed gather: a partial gather renders a stated "partial" note, mirroring `/activity`'s Partial gather handling.
- `tests/try-it-contract-conformance.test.js` and other prose-pinning tests fail when prose moves; run the whole suite (not only touched files) before merge.
- The wrap-up skill text must stay within its size ceiling; put packet detail in the new `_shared` contract and cite it.
- Parent-linked sub-issues keep today's routing (the parent carries the gate) until the feature-level-acceptance record changes it.

**Related:** #4269

Origin: spec #4466 build (final whole-branch review)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md`'s Step 4.0b (#4466) closes a below-floor decomposition parent once its last sub-issue's merge lands. It runs only when a session sees the merge happen: pr-first outcome `merged`, or a successful local-merge push. When the session arms an auto-merge (`armed`) and GitHub merges the PR later, typically on a repo with required checks, no session reaches Step 4.0b. Step 4.0 (closing-links) has the same gap and states "the reconciler does not run the CLI". Recovery is `/claude-tweaks:tidy`'s `parent-gate` backstop row, which stays staged at every autonomy tier. So on required-checks repos, closing a parent below the floor in practice needs a human click.

- [ ] Keep tidy's backstop as the last resort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A below-floor parent whose last sub-issue merges through an armed auto-merge is closed with the `## Closed below the oversight floor` comment, without a human approving a tidy row.

Surface: infra

Origin: reflect hindsight from #4465

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #4596, #2713, #4442, #4492, #4505, #4549, #4554, #4559

## Current State

tidy Step 4's Plan retention (`plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md`, #4465, closed) asks the model to compute, by hand, per plan: a first-add commit date (`git log --diff-filter=A --format=%cs -1 -- {plan}`, `scan-procedures.md:57` on `origin/main`), a 7-day cutoff comparison, a pre-check count against 30, a citation check only once that count reaches 30, an uncited recount, and a decline lookup — across what is by construction 30+ plans (`scan-procedures.md:50-63`).

No `plugin/bin` code computes any of it (probe: `git grep -n -i -e "plans-retention\|plan-retention\|superpowers/plans" origin/main -- plugin/bin` matches only console prefixes (`plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js:88`), policy-schema (`plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js:200`), and unrelated comments; `plugin/bin/plan-retention.js` does not exist). #4465's review returned 22 findings, 12 of them on that one paragraph (density, unstated edges, failure paths, coverage), and its conformance suite (`tests/tidy-plan-retention-conformance.test.js`) can only pin wording, not the arithmetic.

Tidy's Step 4.5 already delegates the comparable worktree/residue arithmetic to `bin/residue.js` (`scan-procedures.md:97`).

## Deliverables

- A `plugin/bin/plan-retention.js` CLI (lib under `plugin/bin/lib/plan-retention/`) that, given the resolved `superpowers-plans-retention` value and the Step 4 table's would-be-Delete list, prints JSON: each plan's route (`delete` / `keep` / `prune-ask` / `prune-archive`), its first-add date or `uncommitted`, and whether the citation check must run.
- `scan-procedures.md` Step 4's Plan retention list cites the CLI for the cutoff/threshold arithmetic and keeps only the policy meaning in prose.
- Unit tests covering the 7-day boundary, the 30 threshold, the uncommitted fail-closed path, and `ask`'s no-cutoff routing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node plugin/bin/plan-retention.js` on a fixture repo with 30 past-cutoff and 1 within-cutoff plan under `keep-forever` routes exactly the 30 to `prune-archive` and the 1 to `keep`.
- With 29 past-cutoff plans it routes all 29 to `keep` and reports `citationCheck: false`.
- An uncommitted plan routes to `keep` under both `keep-forever` and `ask`.
- `scan-procedures.md` Step 4 no longer spells out the `git log --diff-filter=A` date command; it cites the CLI.
- `tests/tidy-plan-retention-conformance.test.js` pins the CLI citation in place of its current `--diff-filter=A` command pin, and `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

/claude-tweaks:tidy computes plan-retention routing with a deterministic helper instead of per-plan prose arithmetic, so large plan archives route consistently.

## Technical Approach

Model the CLI on `plugin/bin/residue.js`: a `run(argv, deps)` seam with an injectable `git` runner, exit `0` on any successful (including degraded) render and `2` only on a malformed invocation. Keep the routing decision a pure function in `plugin/bin/lib/plan-retention/` (inputs: retention value, per-plan first-add date or `uncommitted`, today's date, cited set, decline state) so the 7-day boundary, the 30 threshold, and `ask`'s no-cutoff routing unit-test without a repo; the CLI wrapper does the git probing. Route semantics are the ones `scan-procedures.md:53-56` already states — `prune-after-wrapup` → `delete` unchanged, `ask` → `prune-ask` regardless of age (an uncommitted plan stays `keep`), `keep-forever` → `keep` unless 30 or more uncited past-cutoff plans and no live decline, then `prune-archive` for all of them. AC 1's fixture repo backdates commits via `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`/`GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` in a temp repo.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/plan-retention.js` — new CLI
- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-retention/` — new lib: pure routing function plus the first-add-date probe
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-retention/` — new unit and fixture-repo tests
- `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` — Plan retention cites the CLI
- `tests/tidy-plan-retention-conformance.test.js` — pins the citation; drops the `--diff-filter=A` command pin
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI and its lib directory

## Gotchas

- `tests/tidy-plan-retention-conformance.test.js:116` byte-pins the `git -C "{REPO_ROOT}" log --diff-filter=A --format=%cs -1 -- {plan}` command and `:117` the 7-day sentence; AC 4 removes the command from prose, so update the test in the same change or the suite goes red.
- The citation check (`plan-citation-check.md`) is a model-judged step the CLI cannot perform. The "30 uncited" recount needs the citation results, so the CLI needs either a two-pass shape (first call reports `citationCheck: true` plus the past-cutoff candidates; a second call takes the cited set and recounts) or a cited-set input. Pick one at build and state it in the prose citation.
- Decline memory: today a non-null `decline` or a lookup that exits non-zero routes to `keep` (fail closed). Whether the CLI calls `bin/declined-learning.js lookup` itself or takes the decline state as input, preserve that fail-closed direction.
- The 7-day boundary's exact edge (a plan exactly 7 days old: within or past?) is not stated in today's prose; the unit test fixes it — pick one and state it in the prose so the two cannot drift.
- `%cs` is the committer date in the commit's own timezone; compare dates, not timestamps, or pin the timezone in tests so the boundary test is not flaky across CI's Node 20 runners and local machines.
- A new `plugin/bin/*.js` CLI falls under the repo's bin source-scan conformance suites (spawn options, `--no-optional-locks` on git reads, exit-code conformance) — follow the house CLI wrapper contract from the start.
- #4596 (`ready`, `auto:build`) also edits `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` (a different section — stale-claim checks); expect a rebase if both are in flight.

## Original request

groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Current State

The multi-spec artifact-overwrite completion check (`plugin/skills/flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`, run before the Consolidated Review Console) calls `plugin/bin/check-artifact-overwrite.js`. It finds every `docs/journeys/` or `stories/` path that one commit in the run added and a later commit modified. A hunk with deletions passes only if one of three extension tests in `plugin/bin/lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.js` accepts it: same-spec self-edit, list reflow, or step-markup reformat. Anything else is reported as an overwrite (exit 1), which HARD-GATEs the run.

The same-spec self-edit test (`artifact-overwrite-check.js:310`, `const selfEdit = commitRefs.size > 0 && setsIntersect(commitRefs, blamedRefs)`) attributes commits only through a `refs #N` trailer on the commit message (`extractRefs`, `:85`). Most of the pipeline's commit sites (stories, review fix waves, wrap-up) write no such trailer; only `plugin/skills/build/micro-plan.md:66` asks for `refs #{n}`. In a run where neither commit has a trailer, the test can never match. A spec's own review fix to a story or journey file it added earlier in the same run then trips the HARD-GATE as a false positive, and the run stops for a manual ruling. This is the most common legitimate edit of that kind.

The run already records which spec was running when. Every `spec-status` call appends `{ phase, status, at }` to `specs[].phases[]` in the multi-spec run's `manifest.yml` (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/manifest.js`'s `transitionSpec`, `spec.phases.push({ phase, status, at: nowIso })`), and `startedAt` is set on a spec's first `running` transition. `readManifest(runDir)` is exported from the same module. The check does not read the manifest today.

## Deliverables

- **Manifest-window attribution fallback.** `checkArtifactOverwrite` accepts an optional `manifest` (or `runDir`) input. A commit is attributed to spec ids in this order:
  1. its own `refs #N` trailer, when present (unchanged);
  2. otherwise, the single spec whose manifest window contains the commit's author date. A spec's window runs from its first recorded transition (`startedAt`, else its earliest `phases[].at`) up to the next spec's first recorded transition. The last spec's window is open-ended.
  3. otherwise the commit is unattributed (an empty set, as today).

  The same-spec self-edit test then compares these attributions for the deleting commit and every blamed commit. A commit whose author date falls inside no window, or inside more than one, stays unattributed. The fallback never guesses.
- **CLI flag.** `plugin/bin/check-artifact-overwrite.js` gains an optional `--run <dir>` flag that reads `manifest.yml` from that directory and passes it through. Without the flag, or with no readable manifest there, behavior stays as it is today, refs-only. An unreadable or unparseable manifest named by `--run` is the walk's own failure (exit 3), never a silent fall back to refs-only.
- **Distinct unattributable reason.** When a self-edit judgment fails because the deleting commit or a blamed commit has no attribution from either source, the `overwrites[]` entry's `reason` says so explicitly ("unattributable — no refs trailer and no manifest window"). It must not reuse the "refs trailer does not match" wording, so whoever makes the manual ruling can tell a missing attribution from a confirmed cross-spec deletion. The entry still fails closed: it stays in `overwrites[]`, and the exit code is still 1.
- **Procedure update.** `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`'s invocation passes `--run "{parent}"`, the multi-spec parent run directory that holds `manifest.yml`. Its test-1 description names both attribution sources and their order.
- The module header comment's description of test 1 is updated to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixture: spec A adds `stories/x-A.yaml`, and a later commit inside spec A's manifest window changes one of its lines. Neither commit carries a `refs` trailer. With the manifest supplied, the result is `clean: true`.
- [ ] Fixture: same history, but the modifying commit's author date falls inside spec B's window. The result is still an overwrite: one entry for that path and commit.
- [ ] Fixture: the same untrailered self-edit with no manifest supplied still reports an overwrite. Its `reason` contains `unattributable`, not `refs trailer does not match`.
- [ ] Fixture: a commit with a `refs #N` trailer is attributed by the trailer even when its author date falls in a different spec's manifest window (the trailer takes precedence).
- [ ] Fixture: an author date that falls before every spec's first transition leaves the commit unattributed.
- [ ] `check-artifact-overwrite.js --run <dir>` with no `manifest.yml` in `<dir>` exits 3, and stderr names the missing manifest.
- [ ] Each new attribution test goes red when the manifest fallback is removed.
- [ ] Every existing test in `tests/bin-lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/flow/check-artifact-overwrite-cli.test.js` still passes unchanged.
- [ ] `multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`'s command block includes `--run "{parent}"`, and `tests/multispec-artifact-namespacing-conformance.test.js` passes.

## Release Note

A multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` run no longer stops at the artifact-overwrite gate when a spec's own review fix edits a story or journey file that the same spec added earlier in the run.

## Technical Approach

Attribution becomes a per-commit function that the existing `getRefs` cache wraps. It tries the trailer first, then the manifest window looked up by the commit's author date (`git log -1 --format=%aI {sha}`, fetched alongside `%B` in the same call so the walk does not add a git call per commit). `selfEdit` keeps its current shape over the attribution sets. Parse the manifest with `manifest.js`'s `parseManifestYaml`/`readManifest` rather than adding a second YAML reader. Window computation is a small pure function over `multispec.specs` (ordered by first transition) so it can be unit-tested without git.

Alternatives the record offered, and why they lose:
- **Namespace-suffix attribution** (`-{N}` in the filename): this names the file's owner, not the author of the deleting commit. Spec B editing spec A's `-A` file is exactly the overwrite the check exists to catch, so the suffix cannot separate the self-edit from the real overwrite.
- **Writing `refs #{N}` trailers at every commit site**: the check's stated design (`multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`) is to verify the outcome from git history "rather than trusting that every present-and-future write path" follows a convention. A trailer convention spread across build, stories, review, and wrap-up commit sites, including subagent-authored commits, is that kind of trust. It is also incomplete for commits made before the convention lands.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.js` — manifest-window attribution fallback, the unattributable reason string, and the header comment
- `plugin/bin/check-artifact-overwrite.js` — `--run <dir>` flag, manifest read, and exit 3 on an unreadable manifest
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/manifest.js` — read only; reuse `readManifest`/`parseManifestYaml` (no change expected)
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md` — pass `--run "{parent}"` and describe the two attribution sources
- `tests/bin-lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.test.js` — untrailered self-edit, cross-window, trailer-precedence, and out-of-window fixtures
- `tests/bin-lib/flow/check-artifact-overwrite-cli.test.js` — `--run` flag and missing-manifest exit 3
- `tests/multispec-artifact-namespacing-conformance.test.js` — keep passing against the updated command block

## Gotchas

- Use the commit's **author** date, not the committer date. A rebase or cherry-pick rewrites the committer date to the time of the rewrite, which would move a commit out of its spec's window. The author date is preserved.
- Fixture commits must pin `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` (and `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`) explicitly. Commits made seconds apart in a test otherwise all land in one window, and the cross-window fixture would pass for the wrong reason.
- Manifest windows apply only to a shared-worktree (sequential) multi-spec run. Parallel-wave members build in their own worktrees, so their windows can overlap. The "more than one window, unattributed" rule is what keeps an overlap from being read as a self-edit.
- `#4590` adds two more extension tests (step renumber, reference-preserving `Origin:` line) to the same module and the same procedure doc. It is a sibling change, not a dependency. Whichever lands second rebases its header-comment and doc edits onto the other's.

**Related:** #4590, #3831, #3974, #4353, #4429

## Original request

flow artifact-overwrite check: flags a spec's own review fix as an overwrite when commits carry no refs #N trailer

**Summary:** The multi-spec artifact-overwrite completion check reports a spec's own review-fix edit to its own namespaced artifact as a cross-spec overwrite (a HARD-GATE) whenever the run's commits carry no `refs #N` trailer — which the pipeline's own commit sites never write.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** /claude-tweaks:flow — multi-spec artifact-overwrite completion check (`skills/flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`, `bin/check-artifact-overwrite.js`, `bin/lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.js`)

**Repro steps:**
1. Run a two-spec `/flow` in one shared worktree (specs A then B).
2. Spec A's `/stories` commit adds a namespaced story file, e.g. `stories/x-A.yaml`.
3. Spec A's own review fix wave changes one line in that file (two locator strings updated to match a copy change made in the same commit).
4. None of the run's commits (build, stories, review fix waves) carry a `refs #A` trailer.
5. At end of run, `check-artifact-overwrite.js --base {EXPECTED_BASE} --path docs/journeys/ --path stories/` runs over the run's range.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the edit is recognised as a same-spec self-correction (both commits are spec A's; the manifest phase timestamps put both inside spec A's test/review window, spec B started hours later; the file carries spec A's `-A` namespace suffix), so the check passes.
Actual: exit 1 with one overwrite reported. The "same-spec self-edit" test requires the deleting commit and the blamed commit to share the same `refs #{N}` trailer, so it can never match in a run whose commit sites don't write that trailer. The procedure treats this as a HARD-GATE before the consolidated console, so the run stops for a manual ruling on a false positive — the most common legitimate edit shape (a spec correcting its own artifact during review).

Suggested fixes (any of):
1. When neither commit has a `refs #N` trailer, fall back to spec attribution from the run's `manifest.yml` phase windows (`specs[].phases[].at`), or from the artifact's own `-{N}` namespace suffix (a file namespaced to spec A, modified while spec A is the running spec, is a self-edit).
2. Have the pipeline's commit sites (build, stories, review fix waves, wrap-up) write a `refs #{N}` trailer in multi-spec runs, so the existing test works.
3. At minimum, report "unattributable (no refs trailer)" as its own verdict instead of an overwrite.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.1

Related (different false-positive shape in the same check): #4590.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`integration-model` has no static schema default. When neither the run's `config.yml` pin nor `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` sets it, `detectIntegrationModel` (`plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js:642-659`) computes it from the forge-detection ladder (`plugin/skills/_shared/forge-detection.md`, checks 1 and 3). Verified on `main` at `fed17360e`:

- Line 644 builds one `execOpts` with a hardcoded `timeout: 5000` for both the `git remote get-url origin` probe and the `gh repo view --json owner,name` probe. The project's `gh-timeout-ms` policy key (`policy-schema.js:134`, bounded 1000–60000, default 5000) and the `CLAUDE_TWEAKS_GH_TIMEOUT_MS` env override, which every other direct `gh` call honours through `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js`'s `GH_TIMEOUT_MS` ladder (env > policy > default), are never read here.
- Lines 652-656: any throw from the `gh` probe returns `'local-merge'`. A timeout (the child killed after 5 s) cannot be told apart from a definitive "not authenticated / not a GitHub repo" exit, and nothing records which one happened.
- The function is called in three places: `plugin/bin/lib/policy-derived-defaults.js:45` (behind `bin/resolve-policy.js`'s `integration-model` branch), `resolveIntegrationModel` (`policy-schema.js:670-676`, used by `bin/lib/reconcile/index.js`), and `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js:1659` (`resolveRunPinnedIntegrationModel`, the PR-stamp gate's fallback for a run with no pin yet).

Observed effect (reported against plugin 6.156.3): on a GitHub Enterprise host where `gh` calls routinely take 4–14 s, two unpinned reads of `integration-model` during one `/claude-tweaks:flow #A,#B,#C` run returned `local-merge` and then `pr-first`, both `source: default`. `/build` logged a SKIP of the draft-PR bootstrap, and the bookkeeping-stamps gate then denied the next write (`bookkeeping-stamp-deny`, record-pr) until the run was corrected by hand. A contributing factor is that the first read ran without `--run`, so it bypassed the run-scoped pin (`plugin/skills/_shared/integration-model.md`, "Run-scoped stability"). That caller-side miss is a separate concern. This record covers the detection function: it fails on a slow forge and leaves no trace.

## Deliverables

1. `detectIntegrationModel` bounds its `gh repo view` probe with the resolved `gh` timeout for the repo it is detecting: `CLAUDE_TWEAKS_GH_TIMEOUT_MS` (when valid within the key's bounds) > `gh-timeout-ms` read from `{repoRoot}/.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` > the 5000 ms schema default. This is the same precedence as `shared-primitives.js`'s ladder, but anchored on `repoRoot` rather than `process.cwd()`. An explicit `opts.timeoutMs` passed by a caller wins over the ladder. The `git remote get-url origin` probe keeps a short local bound; it does not need the `gh` budget.
2. A `gh` probe that ends by timeout (`ETIMEDOUT` / killed by signal) is retried once with the same timeout before detection gives up. That matches `gh-timeout-ms`'s documented "killed and retried once" semantics. A definitive outcome is not retried: a non-zero exit, or `gh` absent (`ENOENT`).
3. Detection reports *why* it resolved `local-merge`. A timeout that survives the retry is a **degraded** detection, kept distinct from a detected `local-merge` (no remote, `gh` absent, or `gh repo view` exiting non-zero). Whatever form the signal takes, `detectIntegrationModel(repoRoot, opts)` keeps returning a bare enum string for every existing caller (additive only). Callers that want the reason get it through a new opt-in surface, for example an `opts.onDegrade` callback or a sibling export.
4. `bin/resolve-policy.js`'s `integration-model` resolution (through `policy-derived-defaults.js`) surfaces a degraded detection in two ways: a `degraded — integration-model: forge detection timed out after {ms} ms (x2); resolved local-merge — pin integration-model in .claude-tweaks/policy.yml or raise gh-timeout-ms` line on stderr, and an additive `degraded: "<reason>"` field on that key's JSON entry. `--values` output is unchanged (still the bare value on stdout).
5. `pre-tool-use.js`'s `resolveRunPinnedIntegrationModel` passes an explicit `opts.timeoutMs` chosen so that its worst case (probe plus one retry) stays within the hook's spawn budget (the "I5" budget its own comment cites). A comment at the call site explains why the hook does not inherit a 60 s `gh-timeout-ms`.
6. `plugin/skills/_shared/forge-detection.md`'s "Code twin" paragraph and `detectIntegrationModel`'s header comment (`policy-schema.js:623-641`, which currently says "Each check runs under a 5s timeout") describe the new timeout source, the retry-once rule, and the degraded-vs-detected distinction.
7. Tests in `tests/integration-model.test.js`, `tests/merge-verification.test.js` (which pins `computeDerivedDefaults` today), and `tests/resolve-policy-cli.test.js` cover the new behaviour. Each one must go red against the current code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `gh-timeout-ms: 20000` in a fixture repo's `policy.yml` and a fake `gh` on `PATH` that sleeps 8 s and then prints valid JSON, `detectIntegrationModel(fixture)` returns `pr-first`. Today it returns `local-merge` after 5 s.
- With `CLAUDE_TWEAKS_GH_TIMEOUT_MS=20000` and no policy key, the same fake resolves `pr-first`. With an explicit `opts.timeoutMs: 1000`, it resolves `local-merge` as a degraded detection.
- When the fake `gh` times out on its first call and succeeds on its second, the result is `pr-first`, and the fake records exactly two invocations.
- When the fake `gh` exits non-zero immediately (no timeout), the result is `local-merge`, the fake is invoked exactly once, and no degrade is reported.
- When `gh` is absent from `PATH` and a remote is present, the result is `local-merge` with no degrade, which is today's behaviour for the MCP-only environment. `mcpReachable: true` still short-circuits to `pr-first`.
- When the fake `gh` always times out, `node bin/resolve-policy.js integration-model` (JSON mode, no `--run`, no pin) prints `local-merge` with `source: "default"` and a `degraded` field, and prints exactly one `degraded — integration-model: …` line on stderr. `--values integration-model` prints only `local-merge` on stdout.
- With `integration-model: pr-first` pinned in `policy.yml`, or in `--run`'s `config.yml`, none of the above invokes `gh` at all: the pin still wins outright.
- `resolveRunPinnedIntegrationModel` passes an explicit `timeoutMs`, and a test (or a source-scan assertion) pins that value at or below the hook budget it cites.
- `forge-detection.md`'s Code-twin paragraph and the `detectIntegrationModel` header comment no longer state a fixed 5 s timeout.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Forge detection for `integration-model` now honours `gh-timeout-ms`, retries once on a timeout, and reports a degraded detection instead of silently resolving `local-merge` on a slow GitHub host.

## Technical Approach

Keep `detectIntegrationModel`'s string return and add the reason through an opt-in surface, so no existing caller changes shape (expand-contract). Resolve the timeout inside `policy-schema.js` from `repoRoot`. `readFileSafe` and `resolveValue` already live in that module, so the policy read needs no new dependency. Do not top-level require `./policy`, which itself requires `./policy-schema`, or `./shared-primitives`, whose `GH_TIMEOUT_MS` getter reads `process.cwd()` rather than the repo being detected. Classify the `execFileSync` error: `err.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'` or a set `err.signal` means timeout and is eligible for one retry; `ENOENT` means `gh` is absent, a definitive result; anything else is a definitive non-zero exit. Thread the reason through `computeDerivedDefaults` into the result entry, and have `resolve-policy.js` print the stderr degrade line in the existing `degraded —` style (`bin/verify-run-bookends.js:205`). Tests reuse `tests/integration-model.test.js`'s `gitRepo()` / `ghAbsentPath()` fixtures. Add a fake-`gh` shim directory placed first on `PATH`, configurable for sleep duration, exit code and an invocation counter.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js` — `detectIntegrationModel`: resolved timeout, retry-once on timeout, degrade reason; header comment updated
- `plugin/bin/lib/policy-derived-defaults.js` — carry the degrade reason into the `integration-model` result entry
- `plugin/bin/resolve-policy.js` — emit the stderr `degraded —` line and the additive JSON `degraded` field
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — `resolveRunPinnedIntegrationModel` passes an explicit hook-bounded `timeoutMs`
- `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` — read-only reference for the env > policy > default ladder and bounds (`timeoutFromEnv`, `policyKeyBounds`); change only if a repoRoot-anchored helper is extracted here
- `plugin/skills/_shared/forge-detection.md` — Code-twin paragraph: timeout source, retry, degraded vs detected
- `tests/integration-model.test.js` — fake-`gh` timeout/retry/degrade cases
- `tests/merge-verification.test.js` — `computeDerivedDefaults` degrade-field propagation
- `tests/resolve-policy-cli.test.js` — stderr degrade line and JSON `degraded` field; `--values` unchanged

## Gotchas

- The reporter's `gh-timeout-ms: 90000` is above the key's schema max of 60000 (`policy-schema.js:134`). `resolveValue` silently turns an out-of-range value into the 5000 default, so even after this fix that exact setting still resolves to 5 s. The acceptance tests deliberately use in-range values. Whether an out-of-range timeout should warn is a separate concern and is not changed here.
- The fallback value stays `local-merge` on a degraded detection. `forge-detection.md` documents the ladder as fail-open, and `pr-first` with an unreachable `gh` would fail at the draft-PR bootstrap instead. Run-to-run stability inside a pipeline comes from the run-scoped pin (`_shared/integration-model.md`), which this record leaves untouched. This record makes a failed detection visible and less likely; it does not invent a cross-call cache.
- `pre-tool-use.js` runs inside a lifecycle hook. Inheriting a 60 s `gh-timeout-ms` plus one retry there could exceed the hook's own timeout and break the session-safety invariant in `docs/hooks.md`, so that call site must keep an explicit bound.
- Requiring `./policy` from `policy-schema.js` at module top level creates a require cycle (`policy.js` requires `policy-schema.js`). Read `policy.yml` with `readFileSafe` and `resolveValue` in place, or lazy-require inside the function.
- The live-repo test (`detectIntegrationModel: this repo … resolves a valid enum value`) asserts shape only, so it must not start depending on network latency. Keep every new case on the fake `gh`.

## Original request

policy-schema detectIntegrationModel: ignores gh-timeout-ms and silently falls back to local-merge

**Summary:** Forge detection for `integration-model` uses a hardcoded 5 s `gh repo view` timeout. It ignores the project's `gh-timeout-ms` and silently returns `local-merge` on any failure, so on a slow GitHub Enterprise host the resolved model flips from run to run.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/policy-schema.js` (`detectIntegrationModel`), used by `resolve-policy.js integration-model`

**Repro steps:**
1. Use a project with no `integration-model:` key in `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`. Set `gh-timeout-ms: 90000` because the forge is a GitHub Enterprise host where `gh` calls routinely take 4–14 s.
2. Run `/claude-tweaks:flow #A,#B,#C` (a multi-record run on the default worktree strategy).
3. Resolve `integration-model` once before the worktree catch-up and once again inside the worktree minutes later.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the same model on every resolution. Detection should honour `gh-timeout-ms`; if it can't decide, it should fall back to a stable value with a logged degrade, not silently switch models.
Actual: one read returned `local-merge` and a later read returned `pr-first`. Both came from detection (`source: default`), because the hardcoded `timeout: 5000` (`bin/lib/policy-schema.js:644,652-654`, still present on main at bcd27902c) sometimes fails and falls back to `local-merge` without a trace. `/build` logged a SKIP of the draft-PR bootstrap. The bookkeeping-stamps gate then denied the next write (`bookkeeping-stamp-deny`, record-pr), and a manual correction was needed before the draft PR opened. Contributing factor: the first read ran without `--run`, so it bypassed the Manifesto's run-scoped pin (`_shared/integration-model.md`, "Run-scoped stability").

**Suggested fix:** pass the resolved `gh-timeout-ms` to the detection `gh` call. When detection fails, keep the pinned or default model rather than silently returning `local-merge`, and log a degrade line so that "detected local-merge" can be told apart from "detection failed". Workaround: pin `integration-model:` explicitly in `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.156.3

groups.body:
Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #4502

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/issues/provenance.js`'s `resolveProvenance` gives a record with no `by:*` label the side-effect class named by its body's `Origin:` line. `plugin/bin/lib/issues/trust.js` counts a record whose `Origin:` line ends `from #N` as a corrective follow-up against #N's class. Neither checks who wrote the issue. `by:*` labels need triage access, but anyone who can open an issue in a public repo can write an `Origin:` line.

So in a public consumer repo, an outsider can file an issue whose body starts `Origin: demo changes-requested from #7`. It then counts as a corrective follow-up against #7's trust class, which can flip that class from `clean` to `mixed` and withhold autonomy grants (`autonomy.js`'s `permittedGrants`). It can also add samples to any side-effect class. The direction is mostly toward less autonomy, but class membership becomes forgeable. Found during #4502's brainstorm on 2026-10-30.

In this repo, every one of the 2,847 records was authored by the owner or by an installed app. So there is no observed case, and the exposure is in other public repos that use the plugin.

## Deliverables

1. Decide the rule for issues whose author has no trusted association (`OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, as `comment-trust.js` defines them) and is not an installed app. Either their `Origin:` line is ignored (the record resolves `human:human`), or they are excluded from trust rows entirely. State which in the PR and why.
2. Fetch the author association wherever trust rows are built (the session-scoped record snapshot, `_shared/record-queue-fetch.md`), and pass it to `resolveProvenance` and `trustRows`.
3. Tests for an outsider-authored record with a forged `Origin:` line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An issue whose author association is `NONE` or `CONTRIBUTOR`, with `Origin: demo changes-requested from #7`, adds no follow-up to #7's class and joins no side-effect class.
- The same body from an `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` author, or from an installed app, is unchanged.
- A record fetched without an author association keeps today's behaviour, documented in the PR as the fail-open direction with its reason.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Trust tracking now ignores provenance lines written by people outside the repository.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/provenance.js` (modify)
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/trust.js` (modify)
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/comment-trust.js` (read: the trusted-association set to reuse)
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record-snapshot.js` (modify: carry the author association)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/tidy/approve-mode.md`'s "Archiving the run" archives the run only after Step 7.5's commit lands. `plugin/skills/tidy/step-7-5-worktree-always.md`'s first paragraph skips the worktree, the commit and the PR whenever the approved set holds no working-tree write (an all-`gh` set), and says the run dir's audit files "stay uncommitted at `$RUN_ROOT`". `hooks.js archive-run` then refuses `audit-untracked` (decisions.md, report.md and staged/ are not tracked), so the run can never archive. Its `staged/` still holds the already-applied proposals, so `session-residue.js`'s `collectApprovableStandalone` lists it at every SessionStart ("standalone run(s) finished with unapproved staged proposal(s)"), and `backlog/attention-mode.md`'s tidy row keeps reading "5 tidy proposal(s) staged awaiting approval".

Observed 2026-10-30 on `2026-10-28T172007-sweep-standalone`: `tidy --approve` applied all 7 items (3 digest absorbs into #4405/#4403/#4400, a new settle record #4560, 3 old-value-guarded `update-ref -d` orphan-ref deletions), logged each to decisions.md, closed the run, and `archive-run` refused `audit-untracked`. The same gap has been worked around by hand before. #3409, #3410, #4075 and #4470 each landed a sweep or tidy run's trail through a dedicated PR so the run could archive, so the cost recurs on every forge-only approval.

## Deliverables

1. Record per staged item that `--approve` applied it, in one representation both readers use, so `collectApprovableStandalone` and attention-mode's tidy row stop counting applied items. Examples: move applied items into `staged/applied/`, or a per-item outcome file the detectors read.
2. Give the forge-only approval path a terminal state the residue probe accepts. Either commit the run trail through the existing `pr-first` housekeeping-PR path when the approved set is forge-only, or let `archive-run` accept an untracked trail for a closed run whose every staged item is recorded applied. State in the PR which one and why.
3. Tests for both readers and for the archival outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `tidy --approve` applies every staged item of a forge-only approved set, the next SessionStart does not list that run under unapproved staged proposals, and `backlog attention`'s tidy row omits it.
- That run reaches an archived (or documented terminal) state without a manual git step.
- A run with at least one staged item not yet applied is still listed by both readers.

## Release Note

After `/claude-tweaks:tidy --approve` applies a run's staged items, the session-start notice and `/claude-tweaks:backlog attention` stop reporting them as awaiting approval.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/tidy/approve-mode.md` (modify)
- `plugin/skills/tidy/step-7-5-worktree-always.md` (modify)
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js` (modify)
- `plugin/skills/backlog/attention-mode.md` (modify)
